acceptance: Each of the five patches is adapted, retired as upstreamed with a reviewed reason, or dropped with owner approval, and downstream/patches.json records the outcome.
Patches that conflict with v30.33.0 but are not among these five (if any appear after earlier patches are resolved) are handled the same way and listed in the PR body.
A fork PR refreshing to v30.33.0 merges with every required check green, and benchbox-sqlglot 30.33.0.1 is published by the fork's delivery path.
Any change in generated SQL caused by moving to upstream behaviour (as #89 did for SQLite datesub) is listed in the PR body with before and after output and the engines it was checked on.
BenchBox core adopts 30.33.0.1 through its delivery workflow; the adoption PR is linked in the context.
The controller's refresh issue and drift issues for these patches are closed by the controller, not by hand.
context:
Decision gate: before writing code, compare each conflicting hunk with the upstream change that caused it. If upstream now has an equivalent of the patch's behaviour, propose retirement. If keeping the patch would change generated SQL beyond the patch's recorded intent, or retiring it would change BenchBox query output, get owner approval with before and after SQL for that patch before merging. Adapting a patch with no output change needs no owner decision. Order: drift-probe-stops-at-first-failing-patch-20261117 may land first so issues show all failures, but this item does not wait for it.

Verification rubric: (1) refresh candidate on v30.33.0 replays cleanly after the adaptations; (2) the fork's source checks and engine tests pass on the refresh PR, including tests for each adapted patch; (3) blank_only_hunks finds nothing in the new patches (contract test); (4) the controller's next run reports up-to-date with no drift issues for these five patches; (5) core's adoption PR passes CI and merges.

Guardrails: follow MAINTAINING.md; do not hand-edit normalized patches outside refresh integrate; do not weaken or delete a patch's tests to make it apply; do not skip v30.33.0 for v30.32.0 unless v30.33.0 is unreleasable, and record why if so. Do not contact upstream (tobymao/sqlglot) under this item; upstream offers have their own items and need owner approval. Do not bypass the controller's hold labels or merge rules. This release needs manual work, so it does not satisfy sqlglot-e2e-first-release-certification.
description: Upstream tagged v30.32.0 (2026-11-16 16:00Z) and v30.33.0 (2026-11-17 11:59Z). The fork is still on 30.31.0.1 and BenchBox core has adopted 30.31.0.1. A replay of all carried patches on v30.33.0 (0936dbe9) that continues past failures finds five that do not apply: postgres-exact-division (sqlglot/generators/postgres.py), spark-databricks-regexp-trunc (tests/dialects/test_exasol.py, tests/dialects/test_oracle.py), sqlite-empty-group-by, sqlite-index-null-ordering and sqlite-pivot-lowering (sqlglot/generators/sqlite.py). The controller's next scheduled run will target v30.33.0, stop on the first conflict and open a refresh issue; no new version reaches core until the patches are adapted, retired or dropped. The procedure is the Upstream refresh section of downstream/MAINTAINING.md (refresh candidate, resolve, refresh integrate), as used for 30.31.0 in PR #89.
